text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-83421 -> high-error-rate on synthetic canary group `synth-usw2` (threshold 5 failures / 1m). Probe type: full-serve-check.

pagerduty: New incident created: https://pagerduty.internal/PD-83421 (auto-escalation enabled). Initial trigger: 47 failures in 2m from canary scheduler.

tia: acked. I'm on it, taking primary.

alex_k: reading the probe logs now, seeing a burst of 502/503 for our routed model endpoints, but only from the canary IP pool.

samira: any customer-facing errors reported?

alex_k: searches across user-facing logs for last 30m: no correlated client 5xx spikes, only the synthesized probes failing. downstream telemetry looks stable.

oncall-sre: quick summary pls — is this a probing misconfiguration or actual serving regression?

alex_k: looking at the canary scheduler traces, config shows simultaneous fanout increased to 200 probes last deploy. suspect "thundering probes" causing congestion on the monitoring cluster's egress path.

tia: running quick curl against the canary target from a monitoring pod to reproduce:
```
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null https://synth-probe-usw2.internal/check
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Server: redwood-inference
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2026 20:35:10 GMT
Content-Length: 0
```

alex_k: from kube logs on probe-runner-7: `transport: downstream connection reset` followed by `upstream returned 503`. stack trace shows connection pool exhaustion.

tia: mitigation plan: 1) silence PD alert for 30m while we roll back probe fanout, 2) restart a subset of probe runners to clear pools, 3) temporarily route canaries to standby region if needed.

samira: +1 to rollback fanout. How do we silence PD?

tia: running silence now: `pagerduty-cli incidents snooze PD-83421 --duration 30m`

pagerduty: Incident PD-83421: acknowledged by tia. Silence applied for 30 minutes.

alex_k: executing deploy rollback of monitoring config to previous commit (reduce concurrency from 200 -> 25):
```
kubectl -n monitoring set image deploy/canary-scheduler canary-scheduler=registry.redwood/canary-scheduler:2026-03-09-rc
kubectl rollout status deploy/canary-scheduler -n monitoring
```

oncall-sre: any risk to production traffic with that rollback?

alex_k: none, this only touches monitoring probe scheduler in the monitoring namespace. no prod endpoints changed.

tia: restarted 3 probe-runner pods: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/probe-runner -n monitoring --field-selector metadata.name=probe-runner-7` (done).

alex_k: after restart and fanout rollback, probe error rate dropped from ~80% -> ~3% over 2m.

samira: nice. are we going to re-enable full fanout soon? need postmortem plan.

alex_k: we'll keep conservative concurrency, add circuit-breaker on probe side and backoff jitter to avoid thundering herd. Also add a probe-side health-check for connection pools.

tia: customer impact: none observed. impact status: "synthetic-only". Will update status page: "No customer-facing impact; monitoring canaries experienced elevated failures; mitigation in progress." :white_check_mark:

oncall-sre: handing off to next oncall @samira for 1h follow-up and postmortem ownership. tia please drop notes in the incident doc. :eyes:

samira: taking handoff. I'll gather probe metrics, annotate the commit that bumped concurrency, and open a quick RFC for probe backoff. ETA 2h for postmortem draft.

tia: closing PD incident after monitoring shows stability for 20m. closing now.

pagerduty: Incident PD-83421: resolved by tia.

incident-bot: Thread summary added to incident-tracker: PD-83421 — synthetic canary concurrency surge -> probe runner connection exhaustion -> rollback of scheduler concurrency -> restart probe runners -> no customer impact.

samira: will follow-up with a short postmortem and recommended config guardrails. thanks team. :v:
